Contact

Email is the only channel. There is no phone line and no postal address published here, because we have none to give — an address invented for a footer is worth less than admitting it does not exist.

Email

hello@wattpair.com

Read by a person, not a ticket queue. Replies are not instant, and a message that carries a source document gets answered first.

What is worth sending

A wrong number The most useful mail this site gets. Send the model and region, the field, and the document that contradicts what is published. It gets checked against the source, and if the source wins, the record changes and keeps a note of what moved it.
A specification we could not find Several pages say we have found no published figure. If a manual, a certification filing or a support article has it, that page stops saying so the same week.
A manufacturer correction Brands are welcome to dispute a figure. The bar is the same as for everyone: a document. Corrections are made on the evidence, and no page is edited in exchange for anything.
Partnership and affiliate enquiries Retailer and programme enquiries are welcome. Paid placement, sponsored verdicts, guest posts and link insertions are not — they are declined by policy, not by price.
Something that reads wrong A sentence that misleads, a page that answers a question nobody asked, a control that is unusable on your phone. Specifics beat impressions.

What this address cannot do for you

Product support We do not sell, ship, service or warranty any of the hardware described here. A faulty unit, a missing order or a firmware problem is for the manufacturer or the retailer you bought from.
Medical advice Pages that mention life-support and sleep-therapy equipment describe published electrical requirements only. Whether a particular setup is safe for a particular patient is a question for the device maker and a clinician.
Wiring and code questions Permanent installation, transfer switches and grid connection are governed by local codes and belong to a licensed electrician. The site explains principles and where to look requirements up; it does not sign off on an installation.
Bespoke system design The calculators do the sizing work in public, with their assumptions on the page. There is no private consulting behind them.

Sending a measurement of your own

A measurement has a page of its own: submit a log turns what you observed into a structured block, stamped with the format version it was written against, and lists the routes that carry it — copying the block, a prefilled issue on this site's own public repository, and email on the same switch as the mailbox above. It is still not a form that posts anywhere, and that is not an omission: there is no server behind this site to post to, so the block goes nowhere until you send it, by a route you pick.

A submitted log is held in review until three independent logs of the same pairing agree, and it stays labelled as a reader log after it publishes. Those rules are written out in full on that page, and the tier a figure lands in is defined on the methodology page. A measurement that arrives as an ordinary message instead is still read and kept with its context; it is not published as though it were ours.

What happens to your message

A message is used to answer you and, where it corrects a figure, to record what changed. There is no mailing list to be added to, and nothing you send is passed to a manufacturer or a retailer without you asking for it. The full statement is on the privacy page.

This page carries no retailer links, so there is no commission to disclose on it. Every figure on WattPair is labeled by source tier—official spec, lab measurement, or user log—with its verification date.
